title: Portrait and Parish
premise: Edmund Montrose, an estate lawyer of meticulous reputation, is summoned to the remote parish of Ashen Vale to read the will of Marguerite Hale, a woman who vanished seven years ago and was declared dead. The will is dated three days after her disappearance — legally impossible, physically authentic. As Edmund investigates, Marguerite's diary keeps appearing in his possession with entries written after her vanishing, and one entry names him by name. The trail leads to a parish ledger whose charitable accounts conceal payments to silence a land scandal implicating the village's beloved vicar and its wealthiest family. Edmund discovers Marguerite faked her death to escape them, has been living hidden in the parish as its quiet archivist, and wrote the impossible will to force someone incorruptible enough to expose the truth. In the climax, the conspirators burn the church records with Edmund inside; he escapes with the ledger, Marguerite surrenders her anonymity to testify, and Edmund must choose between closing the case cleanly and protecting the woman who trusted only him.
about_author: O. M. Nakamura is a former probate clerk who spent a decade handling contested estates in rural England before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about paper trails, small parishes, and the lies people file in triplicate.

chapters.title: The Impossible Date
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. A courier delivers a sealed will dated after its author's disappearance, along with a retainer Edmund cannot refuse. He travels to Ashen Vale, noting the village's too-polished welcome. Emotional beat: professional pride curdling into unease as the document proves authentic under his own examination.

chapters.title: Reading of Marguerite Hale
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Before the assembled heirs, Edmund reads a will that leaves everything to 'the one who finds me.' The Hale family reacts with rehearsed grief; the vicar watches Edmund too closely. Emotional beat: the thrill of an elegant puzzle shadowed by the sense of being cast in a role already written.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Sorting Marguerite's effects, Edmund finds her diary — its final entries continue past the disappearance date, describing a man reading her will. The last entry names Montrose. Emotional beat: cold fear; the case has been expecting him all along.

chapters.title: The Vicar's Kindness
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Reverend Callum Ashe offers help and hospitality, steering Edmund toward the theory of a cruel hoax. Edmund notices fresh ink on old parish registers. Emotional beat: warmth offered that feels like a hand on the shoulder guiding him away from something.

chapters.title: A Woman in the Archive
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. In the church crypt archive, Edmund glimpses a veiled woman cataloguing records who vanishes before he can speak to her. The sexton claims no such person works there. Emotional beat: fascination and the first suspicion that Marguerite never left at all.

chapters.title: Ledger Lines
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Studying decades of parish charity ledgers, Edmund finds round-sum payments to a fund with no beneficiaries, signed off by the Hales and countersigned by successive vicars. Emotional beat: the quiet horror of corruption wearing the costume of generosity.

chapters.title: What the Land Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Edmund, with a flashback chapter from Marguerite's diary interleaved. Diary entries reveal she discovered the parish sold common land illegally to cover the Hales' debts, and that trusting the vicar was her fatal mistake. Emotional beat: growing tenderness for a woman he'll never meet — or so he believes.

chapters.title: Dinner with the Hales
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Alistair Hale probes Edmund's findings over an opulent dinner while his daughter Rosamund slips him a warning note: 'Stop reading. Leave.' Emotional beat: the seduction of power and the sting of realizing kindness here is always a transaction.

chapters.title: The Note in His Coat
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Someone searches Edmund's rooms; the diary disappears but reappears days later with a new entry apologizing for the intrusion and warning that the ledger's key is 'in plain sight, where they pray.' Emotional beat: vertigo — he is being protected by the person everyone says is dead.

chapters.title: Plain Sight
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Deciphering the clue, Edmund finds the ledger's true columns encoded in the memorial plaques' dates above the nave. The numbers map to property deeds proving the conspiracy spans forty years. Emotional beat: triumph immediately soured by the knowledge that whoever built this code wanted it found eventually.

chapters.title: Rosamund's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Rosamund admits her father buried a worker's death during the land seizure and paid the parish to keep it silent; Marguerite found the proof. She begs Edmund to burn it. Emotional beat: pity warring with duty — the first heir who seems human.

chapters.title: The Case That Closes Itself
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Alistair offers Edmund a partnership and a blank cheque to declare the will fraudulent. Edmund, tempted for the first time in his career, asks for a night to decide. Emotional beat: self-disgust at how easily his integrity has a price tag.

chapters.title: Midnight in the Crypt
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Following a final diary instruction, Edmund descends into the crypt and meets the archivist — Marguerite Hale, alive, older, unrepentant. She explains the impossible will: she needed a lawyer too stubborn to quit and too honest to buy. Emotional beat: shock giving way to reluctant admiration.

chapters.title: Why She Stayed
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite (her voice, finally). She recounts seven years hiding among the people complicit in her ruin, unable to leave because leaving meant the truth died with the evidence. Emotional beat: the loneliness of belonging somewhere that would destroy you if it knew you.

chapters.title: Two Kinds of Duty
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Marguerite asks him to take the ledger to London; Edmund realizes exposure will also destroy Rosamund and the innocent parishioners. He proposes a narrower path: prosecute the principals, shield the village. Marguerite calls it cowardice dressed as mercy. Emotional beat: love against duty, both unnamed but unmistakable.

chapters.title: The Fire Bell
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. The church burns at dawn. Edmund, retrieving the ledger from the crypt, is trapped as beams collapse; the sexton's face at the door tells him it was no accident. Emotional beat: terror, then fury — they've stopped being subtle, which means he's winning.

chapters.title: Ashes and Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Half-blinded and coughing blood, Edmund realizes the fire destroyed only the decoy copies — Marguerite moved the true ledger the night before, trusting him without telling him. Emotional beat: humiliation transformed into resolve; he was the plan all along.

chapters.title: The Unmasking
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. At the parish council meeting convened to mourn the church, Marguerite walks in alive and names Alistair Hale and Reverend Ashe before the whole village, producing the ledger. Emotional beat: catharsis — seven years of silence breaking like ice.

chapters.title: What Power Pays
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Alistair, cornered, offers to confess everything if Marguerite withdraws the land claims; she refuses, and he turns instead on the vicar, revealing Ashe forged the original burial record. Emotional beat: the corrupt devouring their own — power's loyalty lasts exactly as long as it's useful.

chapters.title: The Will, Amended
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. In chambers, Edmund executes Marguerite's true intent: the estate funds restitution for the displaced families, with Rosamund as trustee. The case closes not as he'd have drafted it, but better. Emotional beat: the satisfaction of a job done right, for once, by his own changed standards.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. The village, initially hostile to the outsider who broke it open, begins to heal; Rosamund thanks him; the sexton is arrested. Marguerite asks Edmund why he stayed when the case was closed. Emotional beat: the answer he gives — 'unfinished business' — fooling neither of them.

chapters.title: Portrait and Parish
chapters.summary: POV Edmund, closing in Marguerite's diary voice. Months later, Edmund hangs his shingle in Ashen Vale; Marguerite, restored to her own name, resumes the archive. Her final diary entry describes a man reading her will — and adds a new line: 'He stayed.' Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace; love chosen freely after duty is done.
